reviews.text:
We have used TAPO security cameras for roughly five years, and over the past year, and issues have become common whenever Apple releases updates. TAPO takes a long time to provide an app update compatible with Apple’s changes. This situation is particularly troublesome because our cameras are offline, owing to TAPO’s failure to provide a suitable update for iOS 27.

Most people contact TAPO to identify the issue, and they may suggest numerous ways to adjust your APPLE product settings. DO NOT DO IT. Although the update involves the Apple device, TAPO is responsible for delivering proper, timely updates that are compatible with your APPLE device. 

It has been a week, and we are still waiting for an update to restore our cameras. As I mentioned, they will advise you to adjust settings and to power down and reset your router and modem. None of that helps. This issue reflects TAPO failing to provide proper updates.

reviews.text:

Then after a few weeks, or a few months, or a few days, it will randomly log you out without you noticing. You stop getting alerts. You won’t have any way of knowing this has happened.

reviews.title: Longtime Kasa User Disappointed with Tapo
reviews.text:
I’ve been using TP-Link Kasa devices for many years. I originally started using Kasa specifically because of its energy-monitoring capabilities and integration with my Sense Energy Monitor. Over the years I’ve added more Kasa devices and have been very happy with the ecosystem.

Unfortunately, as TP-Link has expanded the Tapo product line, purchasing newer Tapo-branded products essentially forces longtime Kasa users to start using a different app.

Tapo will display Kasa devices, but the Kasa app won’t display all Tapo devices. So longtime Kasa customers are essentially being pushed toward Tapo if they want to buy newer TP-Link products.

The problem is that Tapo feels like a step backward in several ways. The app is unnecessarily large and bloated compared with what should be a relatively simple smart-home control app. There is also advertising and promotional content in an app whose primary purpose should be controlling products we already purchased. I don’t want ads or promotions mixed into the interface I use to control devices in my home.

Tapo also removes useful features that Kasa already had. One simple example is custom device images. Kasa lets me upload my own images for plugs and other devices, making it very easy to visually identify what each device controls. Tapo limits me to its built-in icons. These may seem like small features, but when you have a lot of smart-home devices, good organization and quick visual identification matter.

reviews.title: Drop in standards
reviews.text:
TP Link once made great products. They probably still do but since a recent Firmware Update the P110 will not connect to dual band routers. I split bands of our router but still wouldn’t find or connect to our router.
TP Link customer services are too dumb to realise that when you say “My P110 used to work when first connected but after a recent Firmware update it will no longer connect to my router”. They tried to get me to share my router settings in address etc, something which I refused to give. 
They are even to dumb to search the web to find that on sites like Reddit that there are others with the same problem.
In the end I found a dual band smart plug which was so much easier and quicker to set up.

reviews.title: Remove the “01/36” Live View Overlay
reviews.text: I purchased the Tapo C230. The camera quality is good, but the user experience is ruined by the Tapo app. During live view, a “01/36” indicator is displayed directly over the video, in the middle of the image, and there seems to be no way to disable it. For a security camera, it’s absurd to have interface elements covering the live view. Even if the hardware is good, the camera depends on the app, so this issue directly affects everyday use. I regret buying it.

reviews.title: Sabotage?
reviews.text: So this is my finding and support pages bear this out. Memory card in my CT200 is full (that’s another story) and LOOP RECORDING is not working so I want to manually delete all recordings from memory card to clear up space.  Now while there is a BULK delete option it somehow does not actually delete from the memory card. However, apparently bulk delete does work for cloud storage. Now delete from memory card works manually in a one by one basis, it just somehow fails to work if too many items are selected - like in bulk delete cases. In my decades using all sorts of devices it has always been delete is delete regardless how many items you mark for deletion. I find it a curious coincidence this issue works in favour of TP-Link’s cloud option which earns them money.  But that’s just me.

reviews.title: Useless as a monitor. The 5-minute timeout ruins this cameras.
reviews.text:
I am so incredibly frustrated by the forced 5-minute "Continue viewing?" timeout on this app. It is annoying, completely unnecessary, and ruins what could be a great product.

I bought this camera to use as a reliable monitor, but instead, I have to constantly babysit my tablet just to keep the live feed running. Having to endlessly dismiss a notification just to watch my own property is ridiculous.
We should absolutely be able to view our own cameras at will without being forced into some convoluted, tech-heavy workaround with a third-party app just to get a basic continuous stream.

TP-Link needs to patch this immediately. Remove this restriction or give us a clear toggle in the settings to disable it. Until then, do not buy this if you actually want to monitor anything for longer than five minutes.

reviews.title: Following are the major cons of tapo camera and app:
reviews.text:
Following are the major cons of tapo camera and tapo app:
1 You cant download your footage remotely ( on mobile data or on some other wifi network).You must be on the same local network to which your tapo camera is connected.So in emergency, if you are outside your home or workplace and needs to download the footage, you cant.

2. Video download rate is extremely slow.A footage of few MBs takes 5 to 10 minutes to download.

3. If you fixed your tapo camera to a place where you cant access easily, for example on the roof or at a height on the wall and if any issue occurs for which camera requires hard reset, then you will require physical access of camera.Because hard reset button is in the camera.This means you will need a staircase or some manual labour or some technician to hard reset the camera.Moreover reset button is at such place that you will require full unmounting of camera from the roof or wall, then resetting and then again mounting.
Lack of simple software reset is biggest con.Although software reset procedure do exist, but that is very cumbersome and sometimes it works and sometimes it wont and in the end it requires unmounting the camera and then hardware reset and then reconfiguring and then again mounting.Thanks to tplink for making the resetting of camera so user unfriendly.

reviews.title: Great App - Standard Notification Sounds For Critical Alerts is subpar
reviews.text:
I really like the way the app is set up and the way that you can integrate everything into the app. The app is very user-friendly. It’s extremely easy to add things, but the number one thing that deters giving it more than two stars is the fact that there’s no dedicated sound for the Tapo app so whenever there’s an alert, someone breaking into my house or motion detected on a sensitive camera that I want to be alerted for I get a standard notification that could be any of dozens of apps sending me a notification.

For me to give this app more than two stars the developer either needs to add the ability to have different alerts for different things within the Tapo app or there needs to be a dedicated sound that comes with this app that plays when there’s an alert or notification. 

A lot of things I’ve searched online say that it’s not possible because iOS doesn’t allow third-party applications to change notifications, but I have dozens of apps that allow you to set a dedicated notification for that app so that doesn’t make much sense.

I have one app that actually will allow you to set a different alert for each individual notification type so I know that it can be done the developer just has to make it happen and when that happens, this will be a five star app.
